header.tagline: Show-ready audio playback for theatre, radio, events and parties
header.intro: Line up your music and effects, fire each one at the right moment, and keep going when something goes wrong. Free for Windows, macOS and Linux, LivePlay suits a party playlist as well as a full theatre or radio show.
header.screenshotAlt: LivePlay main window with the playlist, cart player and mixer side by side

download.title: Download LivePlay
download.subtitle: Free and open-source. Available for Windows, macOS, and Linux.

macGatekeeper.title: macOS: "LivePlay is damaged and can't be opened"?
macGatekeeper.intro: LivePlay is not yet signed with an Apple Developer certificate, so macOS quarantines it on download. The app is safe — this just means Apple hasn't been paid to notarize it. To open it, remove the quarantine flag once after installing to /Applications:
macGatekeeper.outro: Enter your password when prompted, then launch LivePlay normally. You only need to do this once per install.

winSmartScreen.title: Windows: "Windows protected your PC"?
winSmartScreen.intro: LivePlay isn't yet signed with a certificate Microsoft SmartScreen recognises, so Windows may show a blue "Windows protected your PC" warning when you run the installer. The app is safe — it simply hasn't built up download reputation yet (code signing is on the way).
winSmartScreen.step1: Click "More info" on the warning dialog.
winSmartScreen.step2: Click the "Run anyway" button that appears, then continue the installation normally.
winSmartScreen.outro: If your browser blocked the download instead, choose "Keep" to save the installer first.

contribute.title: Contribute
contribute.subtitle: LivePlay is free and open-source — and always will be.
contribute.freeText: LivePlay is completely free to download and use — no licence fees, no subscriptions, no paywalls. Every feature is available to everyone, with no premium tiers.
contribute.licenseText: LivePlay is released under the GNU AGPL-3.0 licence. In plain terms: you are free to use, study, share and modify it. If you share a modified version — or run it as a network service — you must make your source code available under the same licence, so the whole community keeps benefiting.
contribute.contributeText: Anyone can contribute. Report bugs, suggest features, improve translations or submit code — every contribution is welcome. Head to the GitHub repository to open an issue or a pull request.

groupShow.title: Run your show
groupShow.intro: Everything you need to put a show together and run it with confidence.

playlist.title: Cue It Up, Fire It Off
playlist.description: Drag your music and effects into a playlist of cues, and choose how each one leads into the next: play on, loop or jump. Control the whole running order from your mouse, touchscreen, keyboard or MIDI controller.
points: Play on, loop or jump after every cue
Mouse, touch, keyboard or MIDI
Groups for scenes, acts and sets

cart.title: Instant Sounds and Jingles
cart.description: Keep jingles, stings and announcements a single tap away in the cart player, on named pages of up to 64 carts, ready to fire over whatever else is playing.
points: Fires over whatever is playing
A keyboard shortcut for every cart
Preview in your headphones first

ducking.title: Automatic Ducking
ducking.description: Let announcements and effects dip the music while they play and bring it back smoothly afterwards, or have a cue clear everything else for a clean change of scene. You choose how quickly the music dips and how gently it comes back.

interface.title: Organised Your Way
interface.description: Group cues by scene, act or set, colour-code them, and reorder them whenever the running order changes. Arrange the playlist, cart player and mixer to suit you, tuck away what you don't need, and in the desktop app move the cart player or mixer to a second screen.

showMode.title: Show Mode
showMode.description: Show Mode turns the screen into large, touch-friendly controls and hides everything that could edit the show, so nothing gets changed by accident once the doors open.
points: Large, touch-friendly controls
Editing is locked away
One switch to turn it on

waveform.title: Waveform Trimmer
waveform.description: Trim every sound to exactly the part you want and shape its fades right on the waveform. LivePlay can also trim silence and even out levels for you, so every cue arrives at a consistent volume.

automation.title: Volume Automation
automation.description: Draw the level of a cue right on its waveform. Click to add a point, drag the line to dip the music under a speech or lift it for a chorus, or select a stretch and pull it down in one move. The waveform shows exactly what will be heard, and you can preview from any point in your headphones before the show.
points: Draw levels on the waveform
Select a stretch and pull it down
Preview from any point

properties.title: Fine-Tune Every Cue
properties.description: Name and colour each cue, set its level, choose where it plays, and decide what happens when it starts and ends, all in one place.

missingMedia.title: Find Missing Audio
missingMedia.description: If a file is moved or deleted, LivePlay flags the cue before anyone fires it. Point it at a folder and every missing file is found and relinked by name, or replace one file without losing the cue's settings.
points: Flagged before anyone fires it
Relink a whole show from one folder
Replace a file and keep the settings

youtube.title: YouTube Integration
youtube.description: Pull audio straight from YouTube into your show when you need a track in a hurry. Please make sure you have the rights to use what you download.

firstLaunch.title: Quick Setup
firstLaunch.description: Pick a folder, name your show and start adding sounds. LivePlay keeps your media together with the project, so moving a show to another computer is simple.

groupMixer.title: Mix it properly
groupMixer.intro: A built-in mixer, so music, effects and voices each sit right in the room and nothing unexpected reaches the speakers.

mixer.title: A Real Mixer for Your Show
mixer.description: Give music, effects and announcements their own buses and balance them on channel strips, just as you would on a desk. Route buses into each other, straight to an output or through aux sends, and assign a whole group of cues in one go.
points: Buses with full channel strips
Route between buses or use aux sends
Assign whole groups of cues at once

eqDynamics.title: EQ and Dynamics on Every Bus
eqDynamics.description: Shape every bus with a parametric EQ and a live spectrum analyser, then keep it under control with a gate and a compressor. Stereo buses can be widened or narrowed, with the low end kept solid in the centre.
points: Up to 32 EQ bands with a live analyser
Gate and compressor on every bus
Stereo width with mono-safe bass

limiter.title: Brick-Wall Limiter & Loudness Targets
limiter.description: A brick-wall limiter on every output keeps stray peaks away from the speakers, and the mixer shows you whenever it is working. Pick a loudness target, from broadcast and streaming to live, and the limiter, meters and waveforms all follow it.
points: A limiter on every output
Broadcast, streaming and live targets
Meters and waveforms follow along

meters.title: Broadcast-Grade Metering
meters.description: Accurate real-time meters on every cue, bus and output, in the scale you work in. Their colour zones follow your loudness target, so you can see at a glance whether you are in spec.

preview.title: Headphone Preview and PFL
preview.description: Listen to the next cue, or to any bus, in your headphones without the audience hearing a thing, and check how a mix holds up in mono before it goes out.

routing.title: Hardware Outputs That Travel With You
routing.description: Your show talks to outputs by name, such as Main, Foyer or Sub, and each computer links those names to its own sound cards, several at once if you need them. Take the show to a new venue and LivePlay points out anything missing, so you can remap it in moments.

fades.title: Fades, Loops and Timing
fades.description: Give every cue its own fades, loop ambiences without a seam, and choose whether the next cue crossfades, waits or starts on a marker. Groups show how long they run and how much time is left.

groupEvents.title: Cue the whole room
groupEvents.intro: One cue can start the lights, the video and the mixer. LivePlay keeps the time, so everything lands together.

events.title: Events on the Timeline
events.description: Place events on a cue's waveform to fire a lighting cue over OSC or MIDI Show Control, call a web API, move a fader on an X Air mixer, or start another cue. The server fires each one on its mark, so the show stays in sync even with nobody at the screen.
points: OSC, MIDI, MIDI Show Control and HTTP
Behringer X Air mixers
Start or stop other cues

connections.title: Connections to Your Gear
connections.description: Set up each lighting desk, mixer, MIDI port or web service once per show. LivePlay finds X Air mixers on the network, reads their channel and snapshot names, and caps how loud an event can push a fader.

groupSystem.title: Built to be relied on
groupSystem.intro: From a single laptop to a networked system run by a whole team, LivePlay is designed to keep the show going.

remoteOperation.title: Local or Remote Operation
remoteOperation.description: Run the audio engine on the same computer or on a machine backstage with your audio interfaces, and control everything from anywhere on the network. The sound comes from the engine, not the screen, so the show keeps playing even if a control computer drops out.
points: Engine and screens on separate machines
Keeps playing if a screen drops out
Control it from anywhere on the network

discovery.title: Work Together, Recover Quickly
discovery.description: Screens find LivePlay on the network by themselves, and several people can work on the same show at once, all seeing the same cues. If a connection drops it comes back on its own, and if the engine ever stops it restarts and picks the show back up.

accounts.title: Accounts, Roles and API Tokens
accounts.description: Give your team their own sign-ins, with operators running the show and administrators looking after the system. Show-control tools such as Companion get their own access tokens, and you can move your whole team to another LivePlay server in one go.

settingsPage.title: All Your Settings in One Place
settingsPage.description: All your settings live on one page. Personal preferences such as language and theme follow you to any screen you sign in on, while the show itself sounds the same everywhere.

audioEngine.title: Robust C++ Audio Engine
audioEngine.description: At the heart of LivePlay is a dedicated audio engine that talks directly to your sound hardware on Windows, macOS and Linux. Every cue plays independently, so the same sound can be fired twice at different levels and always behaves as you expect.

ltc.title: SMPTE Timecode
ltc.description: Send SMPTE timecode with your cues, so lighting, video and other equipment can follow your show.

tabs.title: A Tab for Every Act
tabs.description: Split a long show into playlist tabs for each act, scene or set. One Up Next runs across them all, and each tab decides what happens after its last cue: back to the top, on into the next tab, or stop.
points: Name and colour every tab
One show-wide Up Next
Open any tab in its own window

cartPages.title: Pages and Pages of Carts
cartPages.description: Sort your carts into named, colour-coded pages of 4 to 64. Slot keys fire the page you are looking at, and pinned keys fire a favourite sound from any page.
points: 4 to 64 carts on each page
Pop a page out to another screen
Pinned keys work from any page

presets.title: Presets for Your Gear
presets.description: Save "House lights to 40%" once on a connection and use it on any cue. Change the preset and every event using it follows.
points: Named settings for each connection
One change updates every event
Override a single field when you need to

companion.title: Stream Deck Control with Companion
companion.description: LivePlay has an official module for Bitfocus Companion, so a Stream Deck or any other Companion control surface can run your show. Each button shows its cue's name and colour, and fills as the cue plays.
points: GO, cues, carts, Stop All and panic
Mixer mutes, PFL and master level
Live countdowns and progress on the buttons

ports.title: Network Ports
ports.subtitle: If you're running the server and client on different machines, make sure these ports are open on your network and firewall.

control.title: Control Connection
control.description: REST API and WebSocket connection carrying transport commands, project data, routing and live meters between the client and server.

discovery.title: Automatic Discovery
discovery.description: Broadcast and multicast beacon (group 239.255.69.80) that lets clients find LivePlay servers on the local network automatically.

ports.note: A single-machine install needs no configuration — the client and server talk over 127.0.0.1 and the Windows installer adds the firewall rules for you. These ports only matter when separating the control position from the audio hardware across a LAN.

api.title: API & Automation
api.subtitle: Connect LivePlay to your show-control tools.
api.description: Control playback, edit projects and routing, and monitor live state over HTTP and WebSocket. When login is on, give Companion, a show-control system or a script its own API token from Settings, under Accounts, instead of sharing someone's password. The developer reference covers authentication, every endpoint, commands, events and integration examples.

companion.padAlt: Companion buttons for LivePlay during a show: GO with the next cue, the playing cue counting down, Stop All, panic, five carts with one playing, mixer mutes, PFL and master level

hero.eyebrow: Free, open-source sound cue software for Windows, macOS and Linux
hero.title: Every sound, right on cue.

theatre.title: Theatre
theatre.text: Sound effects, underscoring and scene changes, in order and on the line.

radio.title: Radio
radio.text: Beds, jingles and segues, with levels you can trust on air.

events.title: Live events
events.text: Walk-ons, stings and announcements for conferences, awards and stage shows.

parties.title: Parties
parties.text: Line up the music, dip it for the speeches and enjoy the night.

how.title: Up and running in three steps

one.title: Drop in your audio
one.text: Drag in music and effects, or pull a track from YouTube. LivePlay can trim the silence and even out the levels for you.

two.title: Line up your cues
two.text: Put them in running order, group them by scene and choose what each one does next.

three.title: Press Play Next
three.text: Run the whole show from one button, a touchscreen, your keyboard or a MIDI controller.

teaser.title: New in LivePlay {version}
teaser.text: Cues can now run your lights, mixer and video. Long shows get tabs, carts get pages, and you can draw volume right onto the waveform.

index.title: What's new in LivePlay
index.lead: The biggest additions in every release, newest first. New to LivePlay? Take the full feature tour instead.

v26.title: Cue the whole room.
v26.summary: Events for your lights, mixer and video, playlist tabs, cart pages and volume automation.
v26.lead: LivePlay 2.6 reaches beyond the speakers. Cues can now fire your lights, mixer and video from the timeline, long shows fold into tabs, carts spread across pages, and volume can be drawn right onto the waveform.

events.title: One cue. Everything on stage.
events.text: Place events on a cue's waveform and LivePlay fires each one on its mark: a lighting cue, a web request, a fader move on your desk, or another cue. The server keeps the time, so everything lands together even with nobody at the screen.
points: OSC, MIDI, MIDI Show Control and HTTP
Behringer X Air faders, mutes and snapshots
Fire on start, end, pause, resume or at any time

presets.title: Set it once. Use it everywhere.
presets.text: Save the settings you reach for as a named preset on a connection. Point any number of events at it, and when the rig changes, update the preset once.
points: "House lights 40%", ready for any cue
One change updates every event
Override a single field on one event

tabs.title: Long shows, neatly folded.
tabs.text: Give every act, scene or set its own tab. Play Next always fires the one show-wide Up Next and tells you which tab it is on, so you can look ahead without losing your place.
points: Back to the top, on to the next tab, or stop
Move cues between tabs
Open a tab in its own window

pages.title: Room for every sound.
pages.text: Organise your carts into pages for each scene or job. Every page sets its own size and colour, and can follow along or pop out to another screen.
points: 4 to 64 carts per page
Keys for the visible page, or pinned to one cart
Move carts between pages

automation.title: Draw the mix on the waveform.
automation.text: Click to add a point, drag the line to dip the music under a speech or lift it for a chorus. The waveform shows exactly what the audience will hear.
points: Add, drag and remove points
Pull down a whole selection in one move
Preview from any point in your headphones

relink.title: Lost files, found.
relink.text: If a file moves, LivePlay flags the cue before anyone fires it. Point it at a folder and every missing file is matched by name, or swap in a new file and keep the cue exactly as you set it up.
points: Warned before you press play
Relink a whole show from one folder
Replace a file without losing settings

companion.title: Your show on a Stream Deck.
companion.text: LivePlay now has an official module in Bitfocus Companion. Search for LivePlay when you add a connection, and a Stream Deck, web buttons on a tablet or any other Companion surface gets ready-made buttons that follow your show.
points: Cue buttons in your colours that fill as they play
GO, carts, Stop All, panic and the mixer
Connects with an API token when login is on

wholePlaylist.title: A whole playlist in one cart
wholePlaylist.text: Drop a playlist tab on a cart to start it with one tap and watch the time remaining.

duckTimes.title: Ducking at your speed
duckTimes.text: Set how quickly the music dips and how gently it comes back, cue by cue.

stopFades.title: Stop All, your way
stopFades.text: Let Stop All fade each cue over that cue's own Stop fade instead of one fixed time.

stopKey.title: Stop Current Cue key
stopKey.text: Bind a key that stops just the current cue and leaves everything else playing.

openFile.title: Open shows from your files
openFile.text: Double-click a show on Linux too. LivePlay always asks before replacing an open show.

waveformPan.title: Pan with the middle mouse
waveformPan.text: Middle-drag to move around a zoomed waveform.

v26.fixes: more dependable events and connections, playback that no longer stalls on missing media, imports that never overwrite another cue's file, corrected macOS builds (now macOS 13.3 or later), a window that fits beside other apps, and clearer accent colours.

v25.title: A real mixer for your show.
v25.summary: Buses and channel strips, a 32-band EQ, hardware outputs by name and team accounts.
v25.lead: LivePlay 2.5 put a full mixer inside the app. Give music, effects and voices their own strips, shape them properly, and take the same show to any venue.

mixer.title: Every sound gets its own strip.
mixer.text: Create buses for music, effects and announcements and balance them on channel strips, just as you would on a desk. Route them into each other, straight to an output or through aux sends.
points: Master and Preview roles on ordinary buses
Pre- and post-fader aux sends
Assign whole groups in one go

eq.title: Shape it. Hold it.
eq.text: A graph-first parametric EQ with a live spectrum analyser, then a gate and compressor that show what they are doing to the signal.
points: Up to 32 bands of any filter type
Live analyser behind the curve
Stereo width with mono-safe bass

outputs.title: Your show travels. Your routing follows.
outputs.text: Shows talk to outputs by name, and each computer links those names to its own sound cards. At a new venue LivePlay points out what is missing, and you drag a physical output on to fix it.
points: Named outputs, not sound cards
Missing hardware goes silent and says so
Drag-and-drop remapping

workspace.title: Arrange it your way.
workspace.text: Playlist, Cart Player and Mixer all work the same way. Show them, fill the screen with one, tuck them to an edge or move them to another display.
points: One layout model for every pane
Detach panes to a second screen
Comes back the way you left it

accounts.title: A login for everyone on the team.
accounts.text: Give operators and administrators their own sign-ins, see who is connected, and issue API tokens for show-control tools instead of sharing a password.
points: Operator and admin roles
API tokens for tools like Companion
Move your team to another server

fades.title: Transitions with no rough edges.
fades.text: Give every cue its own Stop fade, blend loops back into themselves and make a cue wait before the next one starts.
points: Fades as long as the audio
Seamless loop crossfades
Wait before next

settings.title: One Settings page
settings.text: Every setting in one place, with your personal preferences following you to any screen.

multiEdit.title: Edit many cues at once
multiEdit.text: Change any property across a whole selection of cues.

groupTime.title: Groups know their length
groupTime.text: See how long a group runs and how much is left, even when it is closed.

sends.title: Buses that only send
sends.text: A bus can feed others through sends alone, with no main output of its own.

tray.title: Server in the system tray
tray.text: Run the audio engine quietly in the background, with no console window.

youtubeFormat.title: Choose your YouTube format
youtubeFormat.text: Decide what imported audio is saved as, including WAV.

v25.fixes: Linux offline and older-distro support, a sturdier YouTube import, a header that resizes with the window, user data that always saves, and many mixer and connection fixes.

v24.title: Show control
v24.text: Bitfocus Companion support, plus Cue to Continue and Jump Cue playback actions.

v23.title: Show Mode and honest meters
v23.text: A touchscreen Show Mode, LUFS and true-peak metering, recent projects and configurable numbering.

v22.title: Radio-style segues
v22.text: Start Next markers, a default transition for new tracks and automatic cueing of the next item.

v21.title: Faster imports
v21.text: Import and delete many files at once.

v20.title: A new audio engine
v20.text: A dedicated C++ engine with local or remote operation, loudness targets and automatic server discovery.
